unit.can_do_en: talk about Midsummer and Christmas and give dates.

judge.reason: Millon/Milloin and sun/sinun are only register differences; both ask when your birthday is.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: The fifth of May. And yours?

judge.reason: Same date and question; sun/sinun is a register difference.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text_puhe: Mun on lokakuun kolmas. Eli ylihuomenna!
lines.text_kirja: Minun on lokakuun kolmas. Eli ylihuomenna!
lines.gloss_en: Mine is the third of October. So the day after tomorrow!

judge.reason: Mun/Minun is a register difference; same date and 'day after tomorrow'.
Oikeesti/Oikeasti and Onneks/Onneksi are only register variants; same meaning.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text_puhe: Kiitti! Mä pidän pienet juhlat lauantaina.
lines.text_kirja: Kiitos! Minä pidän pienet juhlat lauantaina.
lines.gloss_en: Thanks! I'm having a small party on Saturday.

judge.reason: Kiitti/Kiitos and mä/minä are register variants; same party plan on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Nice! How old will you be?

judge.reason: Vanhaks/vanhaksi and sä/sinä are register variants; same question.
Kolkyt is the spoken form of kolmekymmentä; both mean thirty.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: A big birthday! We need to celebrate properly.

judge.reason: Pyöreet/Pyöreät is a register variant; same meaning.

forms.why_en: Pitää changes to pidä- and takes -n for 'I': pidän. Pitää juhlat means 'to have a party'.
Pieni becomes pienet to match juhlat: pienet juhlat, 'a small party'.
Juhla always takes -t for a party: juhlat. People say it the same way.
Days take -na for 'on': lauantai becomes lauantaina.

Means 'you' (one person). Spoken: 'sä'.
Täyttää becomes täytä- (tt turns to t) and takes -t for 'you': täytät. It means turning an age.
Speech shortens kolmekymmentä to kolkyt.
Pyöreä becomes pyöreät to match vuodet. Speech turns eä into ee: pyöreet.
Vuosi becomes vuodet for more than one. Pyöreät vuodet is a round birthday.
